title: What earlier attempts learned
preamble: Earlier attempts built this system from an empty starter. What they learned while building it is below, so you don't spend a round finding it again. The starter you get already holds some of it: extraction by section, the critic switch, the row cap and the split of a looping reply. Each line is a lesson, not a rule: when your train measurement disagrees, trust the measurement and say so in your notes.

lessons.text: Graph building by name key, alias key and acronym, with no model, was enough; no attempt improved on it with a model. The starter has the first two; an acronym step goes behind its nominations hook.

lessons.text: Relation filters of every kind: an evidence sentence or span per claim, both ends in one sentence, a minimum mention count per end, a cap per source, a decision-model verifier or gate. Each cost more recall than it bought in precision.

lessons.text: Most missed relations lack an end: extraction never produced one of the two entities, most often a method or a system. Fixing direction or labels is small next to that. Raise relation F1 through mention recall for those types and by cutting fan-out, not by filtering claims. Fan-out is claims that join the subject to entities the article names near it but never relates to it. The claims the article does state about its subject are gold, however many (`task.md`, 1. Extraction).

lessons.text: Held-out documents get every earlier document's entities as `known_entities`, and they can be longer than any train article. Matching known names by substring flooded the prompt with short names that occur everywhere; the starter matches whole key tokens. The stress run in `train.md` (Scoring your work on train) catches both.
